did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with David sitting in his house after the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies. This period of political peace forms the backdrop to his desire to build a house for the LORD.

Did you know? David contrasts the cedar house where he lives with the ark of God, which is dwelling inside a tent. This contrast expresses his concern that his residence is more impressive than the place where the ark dwells.

Did you know? The prophet Nathan initially approves David’s plan, but that same night he receives the word of the LORD, which corrects his response. Thus, the chapter emphasizes that even a prophet must listen to the word of the LORD.

Did you know? The LORD does not command David to build Him a house; instead, He even asks, “Would you build Me a house?” The rest of the passage indicates that David himself is not the one appointed to build the Temple.

Did you know? The LORD describes His presence with Israel since the Exodus as moving in a tent and dwelling place, rather than living permanently in a house. This description emphasizes the LORD’s continual presence with His people.

Did you know? The LORD reminds David of his origins and the journey he has taken—from the pasture and from following the sheep to leading Israel. This highlights God’s choice of David and his transition from shepherd to king.

Did you know? The chapter plays on the meaning of the word “house”: David wanted to build a house for the LORD, but the LORD promises to build David a “house”—that is, to establish a lasting dynasty and kingdom for him.

Did you know? The LORD promises that David’s offspring will arise after him and that one of his sons will build a house for His name. The chapter therefore distinguishes between David’s desire to build the house and the son who will eventually build it.

Did you know? The relationship between the LORD and David’s son is described in terms of a father and son, but it also includes responsibility and discipline: if the son sins, he will be punished with the rod of men and with blows inflicted by human beings.

Did you know? The LORD’s promise includes a house, a kingdom, and a throne that will endure “forever.” In response to this promise, David does not boast; instead, he sits before the LORD and prays with humility and thanksgiving.
